key_insight: CPA-NAMD-extF extends classical-path nonadiabatic molecular dynamics to simulate field-driven electronic responses and reveals fluctuation-sensitive opto-currents in a 2D hybrid perovskite.
engineering_relevance: The method could help analyze finite-temperature photoresponse mechanisms in perovskite solar-cell materials while retaining classical-path computational efficiency.
method: Evolve a first-principles electronic density matrix along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
Include explicit external-field coupling and self-consistent electronic-density updates.
Calculate optical responses and resolve real-space DC current density.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks closely match regular TDDFT for time-dependent dipoles, finite-field currents, and linear optical responses; applications cover crystalline and amorphous SiO₂ and (BA)₂CsPb₂Br₇.
watch_item: Precomputed ionic trajectories retain the classical-path approximation, so field-induced feedback on ionic motion may require additional treatment.
paper_title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
